purpose: Acceptance examples for Step 3 design and later implementation; not a test runner, real dataset, completed audit or frozen research protocol.

conventions.diagnostic_codes: Proposed identifiers; implementation may standardize names while preserving the stated behavior and updating traceability.
conventions.isolation: Start with a valid synthetic fixture and mutate one condition per subcase unless explicitly stated otherwise.
conventions.humans: H1/H2 are fictional human identities used in fixtures; they do not confirm a real reviewer.
conventions.gate_fixture: GATE_VALID is a unit-level aggregate decision input: protocol frozen; explicit valid scope/cutoffs; 40 distinct sampled matters reviewed with completed inventory; 20 strict episodes in 10 independent groups; all their critical slots valid; 950 of 1000 expected applicable cohort slots valid and all 1000 review dispositions finalized; required legal/identity/market coverage gates satisfied; integrity and leakage checks passed; core baselines reproduced. These counts are not a materialized registry.
conventions.slot_fixture: The 100-slot examples test only the slot-completeness function; they do not purport to realize the 40-matter aggregate gate fixture.
conventions.calendar: CAL_SYNTHETIC defines S1=2020-01-06, S2=2020-01-07, S3=2020-01-08, S4=2020-01-09, S5=2020-01-10, opening 09:15 and closing 15:30 at +05:30. It is a fictional test calendar, not a verified exchange calendar.
conventions.timing: Verified exact timestamps are inclusive; date-only publication usable at the next synthetic session open. Authoring/audit timestamps are separate.
conventions.validation_limit: Only catalogue structure and traceability may be checked at this stage. No application behavior has been executed.

scenarios.title: Import boundary rows

records: partly populated real row without ID

scenarios.when: Import with declared example markers

expected.note: Never infer a real row is fictional from an arbitrary row number alone.

scenarios.title: Duplicate episode does not inflate counts
scenarios.when: Append a second conflicting E1 record

expected.rule: All records in a collision are quarantined; no keep-first rule.

scenarios.title: References and parents agree
scenarios.when: Create evidence that links O1 to E1, then separately test a nonexistent order/episode/matter

expected.rule: One mutation per subcase; report the affected key and field.

scenarios.title: Order and evidence IDs are unique
scenarios.when: Duplicate an order ID, then independently duplicate an evidence ID

expected.rule: Quarantine every colliding record and its unusable dependents; extra evidence never creates extra satisfied slots.

scenarios.title: Known positive integer PDF page count
scenarios.when: Independently set page_count to null, 0, -1, 2.5 or 'unknown'

expected.rule: No blank-count bypass even if the page is otherwise numeric.

scenarios.title: PDF locator and provenance are checkable
scenarios.when: Test page 2, then independently page 3, 0, 1.5, null; remove source hash in a separate subcase

expected.note: The invalid URL is a fixture identifier; this case performs no network request. Non-PDF locators need their own designed contract.

scenarios.title: Missing evidence row stays in the denominator
scenarios.when: Delete the five unresolved evidence/disposition rows without changing the expected-slot inventory

expected.rule: Deleting rows does not change expected obligations; if a critical slot is deleted that episode loses strict eligibility.

scenarios.title: Review completion differs from verified evidence
scenarios.when: Calculate shares, then add a redundant support citation to one verified slot

expected.rule: A finalized unresolved disposition counts only as reviewed. Zero expected slots yields unavailable, not 100%.

scenarios.title: Ordinary usable flags and omitted matters cannot produce PASS
scenarios.when: Compute gates; separately omit a selected matter from the reviewed inventory

expected.rule: Manual usable flags and workbook caches are ignored. The omitted matter is still a cohort obligation.

scenarios.title: Human reviewer independence
scenarios.when: Use H1 as auditor under another display name; separately replace H2 by an AI agent

expected.rule: Two labels for one human do not create two reviewers; AI is not a human auditor.

scenarios.title: Reviewed value and registry version agree
scenarios.when: Independently change the evidence value, reference another registry version, or remove a required reviewer date

expected.rule: Typed normalization is explicit; a superseded audit is not silently reused for a changed value.

scenarios.title: Protocol state and mandatory configuration
scenarios.when: Unfreeze protocol; separately keep it frozen but remove C or run scope

expected.rule: Do not infer a collection cutoff from the computer clock.

scenarios.title: Strict counts and independent groups
scenarios.when: Apply each boundary vector independently

expected.rule: Ten matter IDs in nine related groups count as nine independent groups. Gate vectors test the decision function, not invented registry records.

scenarios.title: Assumed claim date cannot inherit early disclosure
scenarios.when: Evaluate strict eligibility

expected.rule: An earlier verified matter/order date does not verify a later supporting claim's availability.

scenarios.title: Post-cutoff support excluded
scenarios.when: Build the release snapshot and rerun with a later computer wall-clock date

expected.rule: Keep the obligation unmet; storing future history is not itself an integrity failure.

scenarios.title: Label readiness from necessary claim supports

episode_disclosure_evidence.passage: Fictional passage explicitly identifying the episode allegation and conduct scope

scenarios.when: Derive disclosure and label readiness

expected.rule: First disclosure uses evidence that actually discloses this episode, not the older identity record. For label readiness choose earliest valid support per critical claim, then the latest across required claims. Redundant later support for A does not delay readiness.

scenarios.title: Timestamp and date-only boundaries
scenarios.when: Query just before and exactly at the verified timestamp, then evaluate the date-only source at S1 close and S2 open

expected.rule: Use the fixture convention, not the host timezone or a guessed real exchange calendar.

scenarios.title: Later public facts preserve earlier views
scenarios.when: Append a genuinely new correction/legal fact made public on January 8 and rebuild the earlier view

expected.rule: Compare immutable releases with the same prior source interpretation; a researcher extraction correction is covered separately by AC19.

scenarios.title: Researcher extraction correction creates a new release
scenarios.when: Correct the extraction in 2026 and generate R2

expected.rule: Audit/authoring time does not replace public time. Do not falsely assert invariance between erroneous and corrected benchmark releases.

scenarios.title: Legal event requires status, source and dates
scenarios.when: Independently remove status, resolvable source, event date, public date or target; separately set legal-history search to unknown

expected.rule: An explicit finalized unknown is a quality/policy limitation, not a fabricated clean history. A missing required structural field is invalid.

scenarios.title: Legal changes affect only declared targets
scenarios.when: Apply the event before and after its public availability

expected.rule: Do not propagate an episode-scoped legal event to the whole matter.

scenarios.title: Historical instrument linkage is time bounded
scenarios.when: Attempt historical linkage using only that later mapping

expected.rule: A current ticker match is insufficient. Venue and valid-time intervals belong in the identity contract.

scenarios.title: Warm-up and market data obey scoring time
scenarios.when: Add a future bar, then separately add the missing permitted past bar; perturb a later corporate-action adjustment

expected.rule: Distinguish full conduct coverage from warm-up coverage. If point-in-time adjustment provenance is unavailable, record a limitation and do not claim verified invariance.

scenarios.title: Frozen frame and deterministic draw
scenarios.when: Repeat draw; then mutate a frame row or a grouping rule after freeze

expected.rule: Record sorting/ranking and replacement rules. This test does not draw a real research sample.

scenarios.title: Input provenance and release manifests
scenarios.when: Run twice; separately mutate an input byte

expected.rule: Operational timestamps may differ; deterministic content and provenance references must agree. A frame-free synthetic run states not applicable explicitly.

scenarios.title: Authoring diagnostics versus run scope
scenarios.when: Append an unreviewed future record; separately append a malformed record known to be outside scope, then one with indeterminate scope

expected.rule: A diagnostic can exist in the global authoring inventory without leaking into an earlier model snapshot.

scenarios.title: Group isolation and fitting boundaries
scenarios.when: Try to split M1/M2 across train/test; independently perturb test labels/prices and future observations; separately set fit cutoff c later than score time t.

expected.rule: Historical labels and transforms must respect fit cutoff c; purge/embargo and matching rules must be explicit before real evaluation.

scenarios.title: Decision precedence and deadline
scenarios.when: Apply each mutation independently

vectors.mutation: leakage test not run and detector evaluation required

expected.rule: A completed registry-only conditional feasibility report may state detector validity unestablished. It cannot claim detector PASS. DRAFT does not suppress diagnostic details.

scenarios.title: Reproducible core baselines

given.dataset: deterministic synthetic time series with explicit training/scoring partitions

scenarios.when: Run statistical scores and Isolation Forest twice

expected.rule: Performance is measured; no hardware-independent speed target is invented.

scenarios.title: Metrics preserve denominators and unknown labels

cluster_subfixture.rule: Consecutive alerted sessions form one cluster; a non-alerted session ends a cluster.

scenarios.when: Calculate metrics; separately set known episodes or scored observations to zero and create an infeasible fitting fold

expected.rule: Count the known episode, matter and group denominators separately. Alerts use the actual prespecified scored universe. Timing is session-index(first matched alert) minus session-index(conduct start); misses stay NOT_DETECTED, not zero delay. Cluster and timing subfixtures are separate from the aggregate count fixture and define synthetic rules only; freeze actual matching/cooldown rules before real evaluation.

scenarios.title: H1 requires a label-dependent intervention
scenarios.when: Attempt H1; then separately supply a feasible label-dependent model and compare runs

expected.rule: A null empirical effect is valid. Using eventual labels only to score already frozen predictions does not itself leak into training.

scenarios.title: Sample fraction is not automatically a frame estimate
scenarios.when: Generate feasibility summary; later provide valid matter-level frame sizes and inclusion probabilities

expected.later_estimator_requires: declared estimand, unit, design weights and matching uncertainty method
expected.rule: Order-listing counts are not eligible matter frame sizes. Episode yields within sampled matter clusters require explicit ratio/cluster treatment; do not silently use 20/40 as a matter estimate.

scenarios.title: Deadline release with unavailable reviewer
scenarios.when: Prepare the local release/report

expected.rule: Deadline delivery status describes unfinished promised work separately from the research decision, which stays DRAFT while unfrozen. No GitHub push or remote publication follows automatically from preparing a release.
